attributes.title: Preregistration: Block V Reflective Self-Modelling - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block V of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block V distinguishes accurate self-monitoring from causal use of self-related representations. It asks whether an artificial agent represents task-relevant facts about its own competence, uncertainty, resources or limitations, and whether intervention on those representations produces selective changes in subsequent control.

Six hypotheses are tested separately. H5.1 evaluates whether active self-monitoring provides selective behavioural benefit when self-related estimates can alter computation or action. H5.2 evaluates recovery after unannounced internal impairment. H5.3 tests direct self-model misinformation followed by correction/rescue. H5.4 tests whether episode-specific monitor correspondence matters beyond the marginal monitor-value distribution. H5.5 separates internally generated capability change from ordinary environmental uncertainty. H5.6 tests whether simpler task-specific or externally supplied-confidence bypasses reproduce the decisive effects without endogenous self-representation.

The core architecture classes are S0 no explicit self-monitor, S1 passive self-monitor, S2 active self-monitor, S3 shuffled/distribution-matched self-monitor control and S4 capacity-matched non-self control. Two serious bypasses are retained: H_ERROR uses recent task error without an explicit self-model, and H_EXTERNAL supplies calibrated self-relevant confidence externally. Development showed that H_EXTERNAL can reproduce the current downstream checking/compute benefit, so successful bypass performance is explicitly allowed to Reduce or Restrict any necessity claim rather than being treated as an anomaly.

Development-only simulations were used to validate implementation, identify defects, strengthen controls and choose prospective thresholds. Those development data are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. The confirmatory study uses twenty separately frozen seeds and confirmatory-only variants that were not executed during development. Six manifests, architecture definitions, interventions, misinformation/correction procedures, estimands and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Reject rules were frozen before confirmatory execution. The execution registry remains closed until this preregistration is public.

A positive result would support only calibrated self-monitoring and causal use of self-related representations within the registered artificial task families. It would not establish subjective experience, phenomenal awareness, sentience, human-like selfhood or conscious introspection.

Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.
